---
title: "Selection and evaluation using posterior draws"
subtitle: "2.18 · after the postrank vignette m6 and theory book, chapter 15"
description: "Discrepancy between risk estimated on selection draws and risk under the exact posterior law."
---

Each repetition draws from a specified posterior distribution, selects a grade report using estimated pairwise
probabilities, and evaluates that fixed report twice. The first evaluation uses the selection draws; the second uses
the exact law. Their signed difference can be positive or negative in an individual repetition. The selected point
identifies the report held fixed in this comparison. Separate discrepancy and regret bounds distinguish error in its
risk estimate from excess risk relative to the exact-law optimum in the same family.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Own draws.** Among these reruns, 33 look worse on their own draws. The followed run instead has gap −.00061: its selection draws make its chosen report look slightly better than the exact law does.
- **Looks worse.** Another selected report from the same experiment has a positive discrepancy. Its gap is +.00072, even though it minimises risk for its own estimated probabilities. A single run need not look optimistic.
- **More draws.** With 4,000 draws per run, the followed gap is −.00025. The cloud and coefficient radius describe the remaining numerical variation. Realized errors need not shrink on every step.
- **Tighter family.** Search the 603 reports with at most three grades. The followed gap is +.00102. Both evaluations still refer to that run's same selected report. The grey intervals show how loose the discrepancy bounds can be.
- **Both scores.** The two scores receive equal weights. The followed gap is −.00322. The discrepancy radius now averages each score's largest pair-error discrepancy with those same weights.

The grey intervals bound the absolute gap of each selected report. The regret readout asks a different question: how much worse its exact-law risk is than the exact-law minimum in the same family. Its bound includes an allowance for numerical optimisation. A small risk difference does not require identical grades.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
These are independent draws from fictional normal posteriors, not repeated observed datasets. “Exact” refers to the declared law. The separate package toy table evaluates each fold's selected report on the other fold; it neither corrects the full-data risk nor checks the fitted model against new observations.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
cf <- postrank_crossfit(postrank_toy, settings=postrank_settings(weights=c(need_A=.6,need_B=.4),tau=.25,G_max=3L), backend="highs")
cf[c("mean_optimism", "mean_abs_optimism")]
```
This reproduces the separate package fold example, not the browser's six-site draws.
:::

Standalone: [open the app](../../embed/chosen-and-judged.html), for example `?S=100&seed=1&run=6`.
